fatal_errors: The proposed 5 at.% Ti intervention does not reconstruct the target intervention, which was equiatomic Re addition to sputtered NbMoTaW films.
The proposed arc-melted and annealed bulk material is microstructurally unlike the target room-temperature-sputtered columnar nanocrystalline films with amorphous grain-boundary regions.

The irradiation conditions do not match: the target used room-temperature 120 keV He2+ implantation at 1 × 10^16 ions/cm², whereas the proposal specifies 10–100 keV and an unsupported fluence boundary up to 1 × 10^17 ions/cm².
No prior evidence supports the claimed Ti-induced ductility increase, irradiation self-healing, quantitative improvements, BCC phase retention, or preservation of properties to 1600 °C.
The experiment does not test the claimed preservation of BCC phase stability or high-temperature mechanical performance.
explanation: The hypothesis broadly addresses room-temperature ductility and helium-irradiation tolerance and includes an untreated NbMoTaW comparator and quantitative falsification thresholds. However, it misses the central Re-alloying intervention, thin-film initial state, exact irradiation conditions, and grain-boundary-mediated mechanism of the target. Its generic lattice-distortion and diffusion argument only weakly overlaps the target mechanism, which depended on Re-induced grain refinement, excess free volume, amorphous boundary regions, and suppression of grain-boundary helium-bubble segregation. The predicted reduction in irradiation hardening is directionally related, but the numerical Ti benefits and broad temperature and fluence limits are unsupported. The proposed tests could compare ductility and hardening, yet omit TEM bubble/segregation measurements, phase verification, and high-temperature testing needed to evaluate the full claim.
